summary: The free realms of the Middle Lands outside the Charters (the gnome holts of Olodor, the elven household of Dunelaeth and the Baelim of the Aenor Forest): how the world finds them, what the land gives, the old defences and the last war, with a branch for each realm (the hidden holts and their luck, the lost kin, the stands).

unseen.name: Unseen
unseen.desc: [ROOT.GetName] lets the world go by on the road outside, and the world, for the most part, does not notice it is there.

unseen_2.name: The Hidden Ways
unseen_2.desc: Every path into [ROOT.GetName] is known to its own folk and to nobody else, and a stranger who finds one usually finds that it goes round in a circle.

parim_friends.name: Friends in Parim
parim_friends.desc: There is a name in Parim that answers letters from [ROOT.GetName], and in the Middle Lands that is worth more than a wall.

near_friends.name: Good Neighbours
near_friends.desc: [ROOT.GetName] knows the folk across its borders by name, and they know it, which keeps the quarrels small.

refuge.name: A Refuge in the War
refuge.desc: Families from the burnt lands sleep under the roofs of [ROOT.GetName], and they work for their bread without being asked.

luck_of_the_holts.name: The Luck of the Holts
luck_of_the_holts.desc: Every holt keeps a pot, and the gnome whose pot is fullest is crowned; luck follows gold given freely, and the holts have always had plenty of both.

luck_of_the_holts_2.name: The King of Tovodor's Luck
luck_of_the_holts_2.desc: The village-kings meet under the king of Tovodor, the pots are full, and the old gnomes say the holts have not been so lucky since before the War of Men.

ill_luck.name: Ill Luck in the Holts
ill_luck.desc: Gold has been taken from the holts, and the gnomes say that ill luck follows taken gold as surely as rain follows cloud, for the taker and for the robbed alike.

holts_luck.name: The Luck of the Gnomes
holts_luck.desc: Gold was carried to the gnome door under the bridge and left there freely, and the masons of Parim swear that nothing has gone wrong for the crown since.

gold_ill_luck.name: Gold Taken from the Gnomes
gold_ill_luck.desc: The crown's men took the gold behind the gnome door, and the masons of Parim will not cut stone on that side of the river any more.

household_of_thamiel.name: The Household of Thamiel
household_of_thamiel.desc: One elven household of a few hundred houses lives in the Kingdom Forests where its dead lie, on the wrong side of the mountains from all its kin.

kin_of_the_east.name: Kin of the East
kin_of_the_east.desc: The household has answered Herrodon at last, and the elves of the Magical Lands have a household that knows every way men use through the mountains.

guides_spirit.name: Guides of the Pass Road
guides_spirit.desc: The guides of Thamiel take travellers to the Kingson Pass for salt and silver, and the forts on both sides of the range pay them for it.

kindred_verse.name: The Western Verse
kindred_verse.desc: The household sings the Kindred Song in its old western form, which the eastern elves find quaint, and stands with the Kindred of the Woods.

hidden_ways_of_the_range.name: The Ways over the Notch
hidden_ways_of_the_range.desc: Guides of Thamiel lead a host by paths that admit only raiders, and the enemy finds banners where he expected snow.

the_stands.name: The Stands
the_stands.desc: The Baelim stand in the oldest wood of the Middle Lands, slow to decide anything and slower to forgive, and no road has ever been cut through them.

stands_awake.name: The Stands Awake
stands_awake.desc: A stand has walked, which no ranger living has seen, and the whole forest listens as it has not listened since the Order sent its woodcutters in.

forest_refuge.name: Under the Stands
forest_refuge.desc: The people of the forest's edge shelter under the great conifers, and the Baelim speak to them in the moot for the first time anyone remembers.

forest_wakes_spirit.name: The Forest Wakes
forest_wakes_spirit.desc: The Baelim have come out of the wood, slowly and without mercy, and the host that burned its edge is learning why no road was ever made through the north coast.

gnome_in_the_bridge.title: A Door Under the Bridge
gnome_in_the_bridge.desc: A mason repairing a pier of the old grey bridges has found a small round door cut into the Stendorler stone, with a brass knocker no bigger than a thumb. The guild says to knock before you cut, the treasury says there is gold behind it, and the master mason is waiting to be told which of them to listen to.

options.name: Leave the door shut, as the masons do.
Leave gold at the door, freely given.
Open it and take what is behind it.

lost_kin_come_home.title: The Lost Kin Ask to Come Home
lost_kin_come_home.desc: The household of [FROM.GetName], which refused the call home after the Ember Lands and has been written in our book as lost ever since, has sent its Eldest over the pass to ask whether the door is still open. She has brought the names of their dead and asks that they be written beside ours.

options.name: Let them keep their graves on the far side.

elf_roads_asked.title: [FROM.GetName] Asks Leave to Use the Roads
elf_roads_asked.desc: The Eldest of [FROM.GetName] has sent a guide to the outer gate, very politely, to ask whether the household may use the lower road past the galleries in winter, when the forest paths are under snow. The gate-wardens remind the hall that no elf has walked its roads since the Iron Charter was sworn.

options.name: No elf walks the hold's roads.
Let the guides use the lower road.

the_baelim_speak.title: The Baelim Speak
the_baelim_speak.desc: Rangers camped at the edge of the great forest have heard the Baelim's low voices for nine nights running, and on the tenth night the voices said something the oldest of them could almost understand. The moots would like to know whether anyone means to answer.

options.name: Leave water at the edge and let the wood be.
Send a ranger in with water and a question.

free_realm_asks_friendship.title: [FROM.GetName] Asks for Parim's Friendship
free_realm_asks_friendship.desc: An envoy of [FROM.GetName], a realm that has never taken the Charters and never quarrelled with the crown either, waits in the antechamber with a modest gift and a request for the crown's friendship. The clerks had to look up where it is.

options.name: Receive them courteously and promise nothing.

focuses.name: Outside the Charters
focuses.desc: [ROOT.GetName] never took the Charters of Parim, and the crown has never quite noticed that it did not. It owes no levies and no tolls to anyone, which is a fine thing until somebody stronger comes asking.

focuses.name: How the World Finds Us
focuses.desc: Sooner or later every hidden folk is found by someone, and the eldest of [ROOT.GetName] would rather choose who it is.

focuses.name: Stay Unseen
focuses.desc: The paths are let grow over, the smoke is kept low, and [ROOT.GetName] goes on living as it always has, out of sight of the roads.

focuses.name: Friends in Parim
focuses.desc: Parim is within reach and the crown is the strongest power in the Middle Lands, so [ROOT.GetName] decides that a friend at court is worth the risk of being remembered there.

focuses.name: The Near Neighbours
focuses.desc: The crown is far and busy, but the folk across the border are near and will still be there next year, so [ROOT.GetName] makes its friends at home.

focuses.name: The Hidden Ways
focuses.desc: Every path into [ROOT.GetName] is learned by its own folk and forgotten by everyone else, and a stranger who finds one tends to find that it brings him back where he started.

focuses.name: An Envoy to Parim
focuses.desc: An envoy goes to the crown with a modest gift and a modest request: that Parim should count [ROOT.GetName] among its friends and stand by it if it is attacked.

focuses.name: Gifts for the Neighbours
focuses.desc: Gifts go over the border to the nearest courts and moots, chosen with care and carried by folk who know which hand to shake first.

focuses.name: A Free Realm
focuses.desc: Hidden, befriended or simply known, [ROOT.GetName] has settled how the world will find it, and it means to stay free of the Charters while it does.

focuses.name: What the Land Gives
focuses.desc: Hills, forest or valley, the land of [ROOT.GetName] has fed its folk since before the Charters, and the eldest think it could feed them better.

focuses.name: Tend the Land
focuses.desc: The work goes into the land itself, its gardens, groves and hidden fields, so that it gives more without anyone outside seeing why.

focuses.name: Trade at the Edge
focuses.desc: Goods are left at the edge of [ROOT.GetName] for the traders of men to collect, and the traders leave a fair price, because they want to come back.

focuses.name: The Edge Markets
focuses.desc: Twice a year a market is held where the realm meets the roads, and the folk of [ROOT.GetName] go home richer and no better known than before.

focuses.name: The Old Defences
focuses.desc: Nobody has made war on [ROOT.GetName] in living memory, and the eldest would like to keep it that way by making sure that anybody who tries regrets it early.

focuses.name: Watchers at the Edge
focuses.desc: Watchers sit in the high branches and on the hilltops along the border, and nothing that walks on the roads goes unseen for long.

focuses.name: The Folk Under Arms
focuses.desc: Every household of [ROOT.GetName] sends someone to drill, and the folk who never fight learn at least how to stand together.

focuses.name: Nobody Passes Uninvited
focuses.desc: The watchers and the drilled folk are joined into one guard of the borders, and a host that comes into [ROOT.GetName] uninvited will meet both.

focuses.name: When the Dead Come
focuses.desc: War has come to the Middle Lands, and the roads past [ROOT.GetName] are full of carts going one way and smoke going the other.

focuses.name: Shelter the Fleeing
focuses.desc: The hidden ways are opened to the families fleeing the war, and [ROOT.GetName] shares its roofs and its bread with folk who did not know it existed a month ago.

focuses.name: Stand with the Living
focuses.desc: [ROOT.GetName] has never taken sides in the quarrels of men, but the dead are no quarrel of men, and its folk go out to stand beside the living.

focuses.name: The Free Realms Endure
focuses.desc: The war has passed over [ROOT.GetName] and left it standing, which is more than can be said for some of the great houses that took the Charters.

focuses.name: The Pots of Tovodor
focuses.desc: Every holt of Olodor keeps a pot of gold, and the gnome whose pot is fullest is crowned. The village-king of Tovodor, the eldest of them, counts the pots this year with more care than usual.

effects.tooltip: The holts' luck is counted in their pots: gold given freely fills them, gold taken empties them.

focuses.name: Each Holt Its Own King
focuses.desc: Every holt keeps its own king and its own secrets, as it always has, and the holts meet under Tovodor only when they are found.

focuses.name: The Kings Meet at Tovodor
focuses.desc: The village-kings walk to Tovodor by night and meet under the eldest of them, which has not happened in living memory, and the hills are suddenly much busier.

focuses.name: Chiromaw Hunts
focuses.desc: The chiromaws of the caves have always been more trouble to the holts than any king of men, and the young gnomes are sent down with lanterns to clear the lower galleries.

focuses.name: The Gold Seams
focuses.desc: The gnomes dig the gold of the Deodolor Hills as they always have, quietly, and this year the seams run richer than the oldest digger can remember.

effects.tooltip: Gold for the pots: the holts' luck rises.

focuses.name: A Door Under the Bridge
focuses.desc: One of the holts has cut its back door into the Stendorler stone under a bridge of Parim, and a mason is about to find it. The kings decide to let him.

focuses.name: Naisa Keeps the Account
focuses.desc: The gnomes honour Naisa above every other power, because she keeps the account of luck, and the holts bring her the first gold of the year.

effects.tooltip: The first gold of the year goes to Naisa: the holts' luck rises.

focuses.name: Luck for the Giver
focuses.desc: Gold brought freely brings luck, and the holts make sure that the luck reaches whoever brought it.

focuses.name: The Tunnels Under Deodolor
focuses.desc: The holts are joined by tunnels under the Deodolor Hills, long enough and secret enough to hide a great many folk who are not gnomes, if the gnomes should choose to.

focuses.name: A Chance to Be Found
focuses.desc: Parim is a day's walk away and growing, and sooner or later a lord of the crown will come up the hills. The kings must decide what he finds.

focuses.name: Found at Last
focuses.desc: The holts let themselves be found. If their luck holds, the world that finds them will be a friendly one; if it does not, the gnomes will know whom to blame.

effects.tooltip: With thirty or more in the holts' pots, the finding goes well; with less, ill luck follows.

focuses.name: Never Found
focuses.desc: The kings close the back doors, let the paths grow over and leave a pot of gold on the quarry ledge for anyone who comes too close, as their grandfathers did.

focuses.name: The King of Tovodor
focuses.desc: The pots are counted and the king of Tovodor is crowned again with a pot of gold, as the first king was, and the holts are as lucky as they have ever been.

focuses.name: The Graves of Thamiel
focuses.desc: The household stayed in the Kingdom Forests when its kin went east, because its dead lie here, and it has kept the graves through three Ages. The Eldest asks the houses what the household is for now.

focuses.name: The Herrodon Letters
focuses.desc: The queen of Herrodon has written twice in an Age to ask the household home. This time the Eldest writes first.

focuses.name: Guides of the Pass Road
focuses.desc: Under the Accord of the Passes the household guides travellers on the road to the Kingson Pass, and the forts on both sides pay it in salt and silver.

focuses.name: Home over the Range
focuses.desc: The household answers Herrodon at last. The houses will go east over the pass to their kin, carrying their dead's names with them, and the Kingdom Forests will be left without guides.

focuses.name: The Guides Stay
focuses.desc: The household stays where its graves are and keeps the pass road, as it has since the Accord, and the Eldest sends Herrodon gifts and no answer.

focuses.name: The Kindred Song
focuses.desc: Elves riding west on the pass road bring word that the Kindred of the Woods has been raised, and the household asks to stand with its kin without leaving its graves.

focuses.name: Kin of Herrodon
focuses.desc: Herrodon takes the household into its book again, and the elves who stayed west teach their kin every way men use through the mountains.

focuses.name: The Notch Guides
focuses.desc: Under the Order the household guided fugitives over the Lunhrim Notch on winter nights, and the old paths are walked again so that nobody forgets them.

focuses.name: The Western Verse
focuses.desc: The household sings its verse of the Kindred Song in the old western form, and the eastern elves, who find it quaint, are surprised to find themselves moved.

focuses.name: A Word with the Dwarves
focuses.desc: The clans of Kunhrim above the forest keep the Iron Charter's rule against elves, and the household keeps off their roads. The Eldest sends a guide to the outer gate to ask whether it must always be so.

focuses.name: Guides for an Army
focuses.desc: The household chooses a side in a war of men for the first time since the Staying, and its guides lead a host over the Lunhrim Notch by paths that admit only raiders.

focuses.name: The Household Endures
focuses.desc: Whether its houses went east, stayed with their graves or stood with the Kindred, the household of Thamiel is still one household, and its Eldest still speaks for it.

focuses.name: The Slow Moot
focuses.desc: The Baelim meet in a moot that nobody outside the forest has ever heard end, and the Eldest of Graulvoa speaks for the stands. Something has made the moot sit longer than usual this year.

focuses.name: Voices in the Wood
focuses.desc: Rangers at the forest's edge hear the Baelim's low voices night after night, and this time the voices are speaking to them.

focuses.name: The Felling Question
focuses.desc: The woodcutters of the edge-villages are cutting closer to the stands every year, and the moot must decide whether any wood of the forest may be taken at all.

focuses.name: Water at the Edge
focuses.desc: The rangers of Selen leave water at the forest's edge in dry summers, and the Baelim, who never thank anyone, let it be known that they have noticed.

focuses.name: No Axe in the Wood
focuses.desc: No axe is lifted inside the forest, not for fallen wood and not for a king, and the moot lets the edge-villages know it in a way they will remember.

focuses.name: Fallen Wood for the Edge
focuses.desc: Men may gather the wood that falls, as the ents of Kilinti let them do, and the edge-villages carry it out on their backs and say thank you to the trees.

focuses.name: The Burnt Edge Remembered
focuses.desc: The Redbark set fire to the forest's eastern edge once, to drive game, and the Baelim came out and pulled their camp trees down. The stands remember, and so do the Redbark.

focuses.name: The Tzikor Clearings
focuses.desc: The tzikor flower in the forest's clearings, moving flowers with thorns and poisoned blossoms, and the Baelim let them spread to every path a host might use.

focuses.name: A Stand That Moves
focuses.desc: For the first time any ranger alive has seen, a whole stand of the Baelim walks, slowly, from the deep wood to the edge, and stops there.

focuses.name: The Eldest Speaks
focuses.desc: The Eldest of Graulvoa speaks to the moots of men at the forest's edge, slowly and in words the oldest rangers can follow, and the Middle Lands learn that the largest forest in them has an opinion.

focuses.name: The Forest Shelters
focuses.desc: When the dead come down from the north, the Baelim let the people of the edge shelter under the stands, and the great wood becomes a refuge for the first time in its history.

focuses.name: The Forest Wakes
focuses.desc: A host has cut or burned the forest's edge, and the Baelim come out of the wood as they did against the Redbark, slowly and without mercy.
